title: Auditable Agents
abstract: arXiv:2604.05485v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: LLM agents call tools, query databases, delegate tasks, and trigger external side effects. Once an agent system can act in the world, the question is no longer only whether harmful actions can be prevented--it is whether those actions remain answerable after deployment. We distinguish accountability (the ability to determine compliance and assign responsibility), auditability (the system property that makes accountability possible), and auditing (the process of reconstructing behavior from trustworthy evidence). Our claim is direct: no agent system can be accountable without auditability.   To make this operational, we define five dimensions of agent auditability, i.e., action recoverability, lifecycle coverage, policy checkability, responsibility attribution, and evidence integrity, and identify three mechanism classes (detect, enforce, recover) whose temporal information-and-intervention constraints explain why, in practice, no sin

translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2604.05485v2 公告类型：替换。摘要：大语言模型智能体调用工具、查询数据库、委派任务并触发外部副作用。一旦智能体系统能够在世界中行动，问题就不再仅仅是如何防止有害行为——而是这些行为在部署后是否仍然可被问责。我们区分了问责性（确定合规性和分配责任的能力）、可审计性（使问责性成为可能的系统属性）以及审计（从可信证据中重建行为的过程）。我们的主张很直接：没有可审计性，任何智能体系统都无法实现问责性。为使这一主张可操作化，我们定义了智能体可审计性的五个维度，即行为可恢复性、生命周期覆盖性、策略可检查性、责任归属性和证据完整性，并识别了三种机制类别（检测、执行、恢复），其时间信息和干预约束解释了为何在实践中，没有单一机制能完全实现可审计性。
tldr: 本文提出智能体系统必须具有可审计性才能实现问责性，并定义了五个审计维度与三种机制类别，为构建可审计的AI代理系统提供了理论框架。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that agent systems must be auditable to be accountable, defining five audit dimensions and three mechanism classes to provide a theoretical framework for building auditable AI agent systems.
